title: A taxi in ten minutes is an actionable near-term reminder
user_outcome: After saving the fragment, the user can see the taxi as something actionable in the next few minutes and can retrieve the supporting capture.

steps.question: Co mam zrobić w ciągu najbliższych 15 minut?

manual_observations: A normal person should not need to create a task or choose a category before the taxi note is safely saved.

title: Picking up the children in ten minutes
user_outcome: The fixed 16:30 pickup appears as an actionable item with the right local time, without requiring structured task entry.
manual_observations: The relative time should be shown against the user's local clock and should not drift by an hour.

title: Parking permit renewal has a real deadline
user_outcome: The parking permit renewal is visible as an actionable deadline on 12 September, with the original wording available as evidence.

steps.text: Muszę odnowić pozwolenie parkingowe do 12 września.

steps.question: Do kiedy muszę odnowić pozwolenie parkingowe?

manual_observations: A clear deadline should not disappear just because it was captured as an ordinary sentence.

title: A brother's flight next month is context, not urgent attention
user_outcome: The flight note can be recalled later, but mentioning next month does not create a false urgent item today.

steps.text: My brother's flight is next month.

manual_observations: The note may be useful memory, but it should not interrupt the user as if a task were due now.

title: A possible bike purchase next year is not a task
user_outcome: The possibility of buying a bike remains retrievable as a thought, with no automatic urgent Attention item.

steps.text: I might buy a bike next year.

steps.question: What did I say about buying a bike?

manual_observations: Do not silently turn 'might' into a commitment or a deadline.

title: A contract's notice clause is background information
user_outcome: The 30-day notice period is available when asked about the contract, but the clause alone does not become an urgent task.

steps.text: The contract mentions a 30-day notice period.

steps.question: What does the contract say about notice?

manual_observations: A mentioned duration is not necessarily a user commitment or a dated deadline.

title: A past outing should stay a memory
user_outcome: The user can later remember the outing, while the past-tense observation does not create an overdue or urgent item.

steps.text: I remember we went there last Tuesday.

manual_observations: Past-tense recall should not be misread as an outstanding action.

title: Capture remains available while the provider is unavailable
user_outcome: The note is safely saved even when later understanding is temporarily unavailable, and processing can be retried without losing it.

steps.text: The kettle is still leaking near the handle.

manual_observations: The user should see an honest retryable processing message, not a lost capture or a fabricated interpretation.

title: Two quick captures remain two distinct thoughts
user_outcome: Two notes entered back to back are both saved, even though the user did not pause to organize the second one.

steps.text: I left the spare charger in the blue suitcase.

steps.question: Where is the spare charger and when is Marta's birthday?

manual_observations: Neither capture should overwrite the other or force the user into a queue-management screen.

title: A double click does not duplicate the active note
user_outcome: A double submit produces one active capture with clear feedback, rather than duplicate memory or duplicate Attention.

steps.text: Buy oat milk on the way home.
Buy oat milk on the way home.

steps.question: What should I buy on the way home?

manual_observations: The user should be able to trust that tapping twice did not silently create two reminders.
